import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.feature_selection import mutual_info_classif
from collections import defaultdict

MAX_DRIVERS = 4

def design(feats):
    # Remove near-duplicates based on correlation
    keep = set(feats.ids)
    corr_pairs = [(a, b) for a, b in [
        ("TPMH13", "EPWQ12B"), ("SCL4", "EPWQ12B"), ("BHKP6", "VWC7B"),
        ("SWH9", "JXR1P"), ("EPWQ12B", "JTJT5B"), ("YZN7L", "EPWQ12B"),
        ("JXR1P", "EPWQ12B"), ("SCL4", "TPMH13"), ("CMUA7", "EPWQ12B"),
        ("EPWQ12B", "CBZ3"), ("TPMH13", "TCN17"), ("ITJ18", "GRPJ12"),
        ("TPMH13", "LRW7"), ("JUM9B", "EPWQ12B"), ("TPMH13", "JTJT5B"),
        ("CMUA7", "TPMH13"), ("JXR1P", "TPMH13"), ("JUM9B", "LRW7"),
        ("VWC7B", "SGR15P"), ("EPWQ12B", "LRW7")
    ] if a in feats.ids and b in feats.ids]
    
    for a, b in corr_pairs:
        if a in keep and b in keep:
            # Keep the one with higher t-statistic
            ta = abs(stats.ttest_ind(feats.x[:, feats.column(a)][feats.y==1], 
                                   feats.x[:, feats.column(a)][feats.y==0]).statistic)
            tb = abs(stats.ttest_ind(feats.x[:, feats.column(b)][feats.y==1], 
                                   feats.x[:, feats.column(b)][feats.y==0]).statistic)
            if ta < tb:
                keep.remove(a)
            else:
                keep.remove(b)
    
    # Filter to keep only non-duplicate features
    keep_ids = tuple(id for id in feats.ids if id in keep)
    
    # Select top features by t-statistic
    t_stats = []
    for fid in keep_ids:
        col = feats.column(fid)
        t_stat = stats.ttest_ind(feats.x[:, col][feats.y==1], 
                               feats.x[:, col][feats.y==0]).statistic
        t_stats.append(abs(t_stat))
    
    # Sort by t-statistic magnitude
    sorted_indices = np.argsort(t_stats)[::-1][:MAX_DRIVERS]
    drivers = tuple(keep_ids[i] for i in sorted_indices if i < len(keep_ids))
    
    # Build columns and products
    columns = keep_ids
    products = []
    
    # Add interaction terms for top drivers
    for i, a in enumerate(drivers):
        for b in drivers[i+1:]:
            products.append((a, b))
    
    # Weighted score: sum of top drivers with weights from t-stats
    loadings = {}
    for i, fid in enumerate(drivers):
        col = feats.column(fid)
        t_stat = stats.ttest_ind(feats.x[:, col][feats.y==1], 
                               feats.x[:, col][feats.y==0]).statistic
        loadings[fid] = abs(t_stat)
    
    return Design(drivers=drivers, columns=columns, products=products, loadings=loadings)
